newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen says to make proposals to ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen says to make proposals to ASEAN.

text.p: Cambodian strongman Hun Sen said on Saturday his government had not changed its policy on solving Cambodia's problems internally but said he would make some proposals to an ASEAN mediation team.

Hun Sen, speaking as a three-man Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) delegation was arriving in Phnom Penh for talks on solving the country's political crisis, said Cambodia had not changed its policy on outside interference.
"Today we negotiate with ASEAN again," Hun Sen told a meeting of graduate teachers. "They come and ask if the government has changed its position -- no," he said.
"Cambodia's internal problems are Cambodian problems," he said.
Diplomatic sources in the capital said the ASEAN mission had received assurances from Phnom Penh that there would be some forward movement at Saturday's talks.
"I will give them some proposals to take back and consider," Hun Sen said. He did no elaborate.
Second Prime Minster Hun Sen ousted his co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh on July 6 after two days of battles in Phnom Penh.
Hun Sen subsequently rejected attempts to mediate in the crisis and warned against any interference by outside powers in Cambodia's affairs.

The ASEAN team arriving on Saturday is made up of the same men who flew to Phnom Penh and tried unsuccessfully to launch a mediation effort two weeks ago -- foreign ministers Ali Alatas of Indonesia, Prachuab Chaiyasan of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines.
The delegation was making a return trip to Phnom Penh after receiving an invitation to come back for more talks from Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot.
Alatas said on Friday the ASEAN team would offer ideas to Hun Sen on ways to resolve the political crisis.
He declined to give details of the proposals.
Cambodia's troubles dominated a recent ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur.
The grouping was thrown into confusion by conflicting signals from Cambodia over whether or not the Hun Sen-controlled government would welcome a mediation effort.
The ASEAN envoys are due to leave Cambodia later on Saturday after talks with Hun Sen and Ung Huot.
